compiler_provenance: Every binary is a release build of the matrix recipe made on stanley with GCC 15.3.0, clang 23.1.0git, LLD 23.1.1 and rustc 1.99.1, and every build-config.json equals build-config.json here. The binaries were copied to forge as zstd files whose sha256 matched on both hosts, and forge built nothing. binaries-zst.sha256 holds the hashes of the compressed files, which equal those of every pair's bin-A.zst and bin-B.zst on forge, and forge's decompressed cc94ac7f and 71c277b0 hashes equal binaries.sha256.
settings: Each pair directory's run.env holds its rounds, requests per round, warm-up, Rayon threads, server and client CPUs, idle spinners and execution mode. Pairs at one thread pin the server to CPU 2 and the client to CPU 4 with idle spinners. Pairs at 12 threads give the server CPUs 0 to 11 and the client CPU 12 without spinners.
lock: forge-backlog-stage3.service held ~/lanes/.bench.lock and ~/lanes/.heavy.lock for all eleven pairs, from 08:25 to 15:26 UTC on 2026-11-19, and refused to start while rustc, cargo, sparkles or another engine ran.
verdict_rule: X14 SPEC D4 when both arm medians are under 0.3 ms: the query passes when the upper end of the 95% t interval of the mean log round ratio is at most 1.02, or its median added server time is at most 0.5 us. Otherwise a ratio of 1.05 or more fails, and a ratio below 1.05 that is slower in every round is a confirmed cost that needs a roadmap row. analyze.py's d4 field holds only the ratio test above 0.3 ms, so verdict.py derives the combined verdict in verdict.txt from pinned-summary.json.
statistics: ratio is the median of all B exec samples over the median of all A exec samples, computed by analyze.py, whose output is pinned-summary.json and pinned-summary.txt.
attribution: attribution/ holds per-request instruction counts on stanley (scripts/request-insn.py, streaming, one thread, 1.05M) across the matrix builds and across cached screen builds of another toolchain, and user-space perf profiles of the matrix builds on stanley's performance cores. Counts locate a cost and profiles name the code, and neither sizes it. Stanley carried other work during both, so its cycle and time ratios are not measurements.
harness: ab3.sh copies nsc-bench-remote.sh into each pair directory and runs it. The copy here is that file, byte-identical to scripts/nsc-bench-remote.sh at 8baa5686.
answer_check: answers.tsv holds, for each arm and query, the row count and a hash of the sorted TSV answer of one untimed request, and a fifth column from bench-gate.py order-digest. For ORDER BY, keys: hashes the projected sort keys in returned order, and rows: hashes the entire rows in returned order when those keys are unavailable. The unordered checks record distinct: for the distinct-row count and schema: for the schema hash. For triple exports checked with --data, missing: counts distinct returned triples absent from the input dataset. Every entry matches across the two arms of every pair. WARM_DIGEST was not set, so the timed native JSON responses were not checked.
